code:
(define plusminus
  (lambda (a b)
    ((lambda (x y) (list (+ x y) (- x y)))
     a b)))

(plusminus 6 2)              ; (8 4)
description: See how an anonymous lambda in the operator position of a call binds local parameters and builds a two-element list.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Lines 1-2 bind `plusminus` to an outer `(lambda (a b) ...)` that accepts two arguments `a` and `b`.
Lines 3-4 place an anonymous function `(lambda (x y) (list (+ x y) (- x y)))` directly in the operator position of a call. They pass `a` and `b` as its arguments.

Notice the double opening parenthesis `((lambda (x y) ...)` on line 3. The inner `(lambda ...)` constructs a procedure value. The outer `(` immediately calls that procedure with `a` and `b` from line 4.

steps.answer: `x` is bound to `6` and `y` is bound to `2`, so `(+ x y)` is `8` and `(- x y)` is `4`. `(list (+ x y) (- x y))` returns `(8 4)`.
steps.question: When `(plusminus 6 2)` runs on line 6, what values are bound to `x` and `y` in the inner lambda? What list does `(list (+ x y) (- x y))` return?

title: Applying an Anonymous Lambda Immediately in plusminus
